title: The sector speaks
summary: The game gets its sound: every effect for the pirates, ships, stations and planet surfaces is synthesised from scratch, three ambient tracks follow you from the title screen to space and the planets, ships explode with their size, and the story is spoken - each character in their own neural voice. The main quest now starts with Kilon Alios on Thalassa, with his portrait in the dialogue box and a glowing bulb over every quest giver. The economy was rebalanced: your trades move prices, pirate bounties more than doubled, the permanent shortage is gone and the starting ship's trade-in is fair. Side quests became missions - many more, in reputation tiers, the locked ones greyed out. The maps have fog of war; right-click scans asteroids and the system; neutral ships are followed on the first click and attacked on the second, smoothly; the hold limits mining; buildings are furnished, with chests, lockers and vaults to open and your Minoan armchair; doors open closer, with sound; nebulae no longer cover planets. The Patcher gained versions and explanation bubbles, and two Blender models were built for later.

steps.title: The game gets sound
steps.text: The game had no audio at all. Now every sound is synthesised from scratch with numpy - oscillators with pitch sweeps, filtered noise, metal partials, formant voices - and seeded, so the same takes come out every run: 117 effects for the pirates, ships, stations and planet surfaces. Each take was measured (level, brightness, clicks) and rebalanced where it stood out. Sfx plays a random take at +-6 % pitch, fading with distance from the camera, and caps how many play at once.

steps.title: Three ambient tracks
steps.text: tools/music_gen.py composes and synthesises three two-minute ambient electronic tracks: one for the title screen and Talos, one for space, one for planet surfaces. Each is a seamless loop - its last 12 seconds are folded back onto the start, so reverb and long notes ring across the loop point. The Music autoload picks the track from the scene and crossfades between them.

steps.title: Ships explode with their size
steps.text: Ships no longer share the explosion used for missile impacts. Effects.ship_sound picks one of three ship explosions from the ship's hull plus shields - small fighters crack and burst, frigates and capital ships detonate deep and groan apart - and your own ship's death has its own sound: the reactor whining up before the blast.

steps.title: Kilon Alios gives the main quest
steps.text: The main quest now starts on Thalassa: Kilon Alios stands by the landing pad, cut from your 8-view sheet, and turns to face you as you come near. Click him and you walk up and talk - his portrait in the dialogue box - and he offers the quest (Accept / Not now). A glowing yellow bulb bobs over every quest giver, including stations while you have room for another mission.

steps.title: The story is spoken
steps.text: Every main-quest line and all of Kilon's lines are recorded with Piper, a neural text-to-speech, in a voice per character (pitched and coloured with ffmpeg) and levelled to the same loudness. The dialogue box plays each line's recording as it appears and stops when you move on. Recordings are found by a hash of the speaker and the line, so re-running the tool records only what changed. (These replace a first try with numpy robot voices.)

steps.title: Trading leaves a footprint; bounties pay
steps.text: Trading paid 25 to 35 times more than fighting. Now every unit you buy pushes a station's price up 0.3 % and every unit you sell pushes it down, twice as hard on goods it's short of, fading over a few minutes - so dumping a full hold at one station pays less than spreading it. Pirate bounties more than doubled, and Pirate Sweep missions pay twice as much per kill.

steps.title: The end of the permanent shortage
steps.text: A third of all station stocks sat at zero for good, and food was missing almost everywhere. Six measured fixes - balanced production, starving stations using less, slower rates traders can keep up with, NPC supply contracts for what a station lacks, and a farm, mine or refinery in every system - brought empty stocks from 30 % to 7 % and median prices back to their base. The shipyard's trade-in is now 80 % of what you paid, so the starting ship no longer buys you a free upgrade.

steps.title: Missions in four tiers
steps.text: Side quests are now missions, and there are many more: eight offers at every station, five active at once, in six kinds - including supply runs and surveys of uncharted points in the fog. Each has a tier needing a reputation with the station's empire; finishing one raises it, opening better-paid tiers. Missions you haven't the reputation for are greyed out with a disabled Accept and say what they need.

steps.title: Fog of war
steps.text: The planet map, the minimap and the system map start dark and clear where you've been. FogOfWar keeps a grid of how well each patch has been seen, revealed in soft-edged circles round you and drawn as a smoothed texture over the map. Buildings, people, stations, planets and asteroids in the dark aren't drawn or clickable. The fog is saved per planet and per system; old saves load fully charted.

steps.title: The ship's scanner
steps.text: Right-click in space now scans. On an asteroid a fan of laser light sweeps across it, then the rock stays highlighted with its type and the ore left in it (kept in your save). On empty space, rings of energy pulse out from the ship - and only then does the radar show its arrows to stations and planets, for 10 seconds. The old right-click menu moved to Shift + right-click.

steps.title: Following a ship
steps.text: Neutral ships are no longer attacked by accident: the first click makes your ship follow them, a second click attacks. Following is one continuous motion: you match the other ship's velocity and ease toward a spot 260 behind it. That spot turns behind it only gradually and only while it's really travelling, so a ship hovering in place no longer swings you back and forth.

steps.title: The hold limits mining
steps.text: Mining used to pour ore into your hold with no check. Now the mining beam stops when the hold is full - counting the ore already flying to you - and tells you to sell. Cargo pickups stay floating until you have room; credits and other items still come in.

steps.title: Furnished buildings
steps.text: Buildings are furnished, the same each visit: palaces with tables, closets, bookshelves and chests; warehouses with lockers, crates and vaults; temples with scroll racks and offering tables - standing against the back walls, blocking walking, never in doorways or on stairs. Chests, lockers and vaults open once each for credits or items, with their own sounds. Chairs are your Minoan armchair, scaled to the people.

steps.title: Doors with a sound, opening closer
steps.text: Sliding doors open only when you're near them - 95 pixels instead of 170 - and a little faster, and each opening and closing is heard: a pneumatic hiss and the motor whirring the panels apart, then the motor, a clunk and the seal on the way back. steps.text: A galaxy nebula was drawn over Kronos. z_index adds up through the parents: planets sit under their solar system at -16 and add their own -15, which put them at -31 - below the nebula layer at -20. steps.title: The Patcher: versions and bubbles
steps.text: The Patcher's list is now a tree: versions group patches, each version with its own summary and a page per patch. Version 0.1 gathers the first three. The code review lists code files first, and explanation bubbles sit in the empty space beside the code, each pointing at a line and saying how that part works; the three earlier patches got 149 of them.

steps.text: Two models built entirely in geometry nodes by scripts, for later: the pirate's hat, with a sculpted skull and liquid gold running over it, and the AAD-73 rifle from your reference picture, its emblem traced from the image itself and the whole gun split into 25 parts. review.intro: Patch 0004 brings the game's sound (effects, music, spoken story), Kilon Alios and quest bulbs, the economy rebalance, missions in reputation tiers, fog of war, the ship's scanner, following ships, the hold limiting mining, furnished buildings, doors with sound, the nebula fix, and the Patcher's versions and bubbles. @@ -1,0 +1,815 @@ 
+"""The pirate's rifle "AAD-73", modelled from ~/Downloads/gun2.png (a side view,
+muzzle to the left) entirely with geometry nodes: one object, "Gun", whose
+geometry all comes from the node tree "Gun" on an empty mesh.
+
+The reference is a side view, so the model is laid out on it: every
+measurement below is in the reference's pixels (2000 x 667 display size;
+x right, y down) and converted with K metres per pixel - the gun is about
+0.75 m long. The muzzle points to -X, the side shown in the reference faces -Y
+(towards the camera), up is +Z.
+
+How the nodes build it:
+  slabs     flat parts (receiver, stock, grip, magazine, side plates, mounts)
+            are polygons traced off the reference: a Curve Circle with one
+            point per corner, each point set from an Index Switch, filled,
+            extruded through the gun's thickness and capped; the receiver,
+            stock, grip and magazine are rounded off through a distance field
+            (eroded then grown back: soft edges like cast metal).
+  round     barrel, shroud, bands, scope tubes, turrets - cylinders and cones;
+            the shroud's slots are cut out through a distance field.
+  glow      the yellow energy cell under the barrel, the cyan charge
+            segments in the receiver window (emissive).
+  details   the "AAD-73" plate (String to Curves, filled and extruded), the
+            hazard stripes, rivets (instanced along the edges), the trigger
+            (a swept curve), the skull-and-octopus emblem on the stock (a
+            skull and six curling tentacles, swept curves), the scope rings.
+  drips     three drops of molten gold hanging from the under-barrel rail.
+Materials: worn red-pink paint with rust and chips, copper, dark gunmetal,
+brass, rubber (the grip), the two glows, gold.
+
+  blender -b --factory-startup --python external/blender/gun2/build_gun.py
+Saves external/blender/gun2/gun2.blend and preview renders (preview_*.png,
+preview_vs_reference.png).
+"""
+import math
+import os
+
+import bpy
+
+HERE = "/home/kilon/MEGA/Dimitris/godot/space-atrapos/external/blender/gun2"
+REF = os.path.expanduser("~/Downloads/gun2.png")
+K = 0.0005                  # metres per reference pixel
+CX, CY = 1000.0, 334.0      # the reference pixel at the origin
+EMBLEM = (1494, 207, 1612, 312)   # the emblem on the stock, in the reference (x0, y0, x1, y1)
+EMBLEM_RES = 4.0                  # grid points per reference pixel when tracing it
+PARTS = []                        # the parts' names (filled by build())
+EMBLEM_MIN = 600                  # traced pieces smaller than this (grid cells) are specks, dropped
+
+
+def P(x, y):
+    """A reference pixel (x right, y down) -> (X, Z) in metres."""
+    return ((x - CX) * K, (CY - y) * K)
+
+
+# --- node helpers ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+class G:
+    def __init__(self, tree):
+        self.t = tree
+        self.n = 0
+
+    def node(self, kind, **props):
+        n = self.t.nodes.new(kind)
+        for k, v in props.items():
+            setattr(n, k, v)
+        n.location = (40 * (self.n % 60), -40 * (self.n // 60))
+        self.n += 1
+        return n
+
+    def link(self, a, b):
+        self.t.links.new(a, b)
+
+    def _set(self, sock, v):
+        if isinstance(v, (int, float, tuple, list, bool)) or v is None:
+            if v is not None:
+                sock.default_value = v
+        else:
+            self.link(v, sock)
+
+    def math(self, op, a, b=None):
+        n = self.node("ShaderNodeMath", operation=op)
+        self._set(n.inputs[0], a)
+        if b is not None:
+            self._set(n.inputs[1], b)
+        return n.outputs[0]
+
+    def vmath(self, op, a, b=None):
+        n = self.node("ShaderNodeVectorMath", operation=op)
+        self._set(n.inputs[0], a)
+        if b is not None:
+            if op == "SCALE":
+                self._set(n.inputs[3], b)
+            else:
+                self._set(n.inputs[1], b)
+        return n.outputs[0]
+
+    def combine(self, x, y, z):
+        n = self.node("ShaderNodeCombineXYZ")
+        for i, v in enumerate((x, y, z)):
+            self._set(n.inputs[i], v)
+        return n.outputs[0]
+
+    def separate(self, v):
+        n = self.node("ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ")
+        self.link(v, n.inputs[0])
+        return n.outputs[0], n.outputs[1], n.outputs[2]
+
+    def pos(self):
+        return self.node("GeometryNodeInputPosition").outputs[0]
+
+    def transform(self, geo, loc=(0, 0, 0), rot=(0, 0, 0), scale=(1, 1, 1)):
+        n = self.node("GeometryNodeTransform")
+        self.link(geo, n.inputs["Geometry"])
+        n.inputs["Translation"].default_value = loc
+        n.inputs["Rotation"].default_value = rot
+        n.inputs["Scale"].default_value = scale
+        return n.outputs[0]
+
+    def join(self, *geos):
+        n = self.node("GeometryNodeJoinGeometry")
+        for g in reversed(geos):
+            self.link(g, n.inputs[0])
+        return n.outputs[0]
+
+    def material(self, geo, mat):
+        n = self.node("GeometryNodeSetMaterial")
+        self.link(geo, n.inputs["Geometry"])
+        n.inputs["Material"].default_value = mat
+        return n.outputs[0]
+
+    def smooth(self, geo, angle=None):
+        n = self.node("GeometryNodeSetShadeSmooth")
+        self.link(geo, n.inputs["Geometry"])
+        if angle is not None:   # (sharp where faces meet at more than `angle`)
+            ea = self.node("GeometryNodeInputMeshEdgeAngle")
+            n.domain = "EDGE"
+            self.link(self.math("LESS_THAN", ea.outputs["Unsigned Angle"], math.radians(angle)), n.inputs["Shade Smooth"])
+        return n.outputs[0]
+
+    def merge(self, geo, d=1e-5):
+        n = self.node("GeometryNodeMergeByDistance")
+        self.link(geo, n.inputs["Geometry"])
+        n.inputs["Distance"].default_value = d
+        return n.outputs[0]
+
+    # --- shapes ------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    def polygon_curve(self, pts):
+        """A closed curve through reference pixels pts (in the XY plane: X, Z-as-Y)."""
+        c = self.node("GeometryNodeCurvePrimitiveCircle")
+        c.inputs["Resolution"].default_value = len(pts)
+        sw = self.node("GeometryNodeIndexSwitch", data_type="VECTOR")
+        while len(sw.index_switch_items) < len(pts):
+            sw.index_switch_items.new()
+        self.link(self.node("GeometryNodeInputIndex").outputs[0], sw.inputs["Index"])
+        for i, (x, y) in enumerate(pts):
+            X, Z = P(x, y)
+            sw.inputs[str(i)].default_value = (X, Z, 0.0)
+        sp = self.node("GeometryNodeSetPosition")
+        self.link(c.outputs["Curve"], sp.inputs["Geometry"])
+        self.link(sw.outputs[0], sp.inputs["Position"])
+        return sp.outputs[0]
+
+    def slab_from_curve(self, curve, y0, y1):
+        """A filled outline extruded from depth y0 to y1 (metres), capped both sides."""
+        f = self.node("GeometryNodeFillCurve")
+        self.link(curve, f.inputs["Curve"])
+        f.inputs["Mode"].default_value = "N-gons"
+        base = self.transform(f.outputs[0], loc=(0, 0, -y1))   # (turned below: depth z -> Y = -z)
+        ex = self.node("GeometryNodeExtrudeMesh")
+        self.link(base, ex.inputs["Mesh"])
+        self.link(self.combine(0.0, 0.0, y1 - y0), ex.inputs["Offset"])
+        ex.inputs["Offset Scale"].default_value = 1.0
+        ex.inputs["Individual"].default_value = False
+        flip = self.node("GeometryNodeFlipFaces")
+        self.link(base, flip.inputs["Mesh"])
+        solid = self.merge(self.join(ex.outputs["Mesh"], flip.outputs[0]))
+        # (built in X / Z-as-Y / depth-as-Z: turned so height is Z and depth Y, y0..y1)
+        return self.transform(solid, rot=(math.pi / 2, 0, 0))
+
+    def slab(self, pts, depth_px, centre_px=0.0):
+        """A polygon traced off the reference (pixels), depth_px thick, centred
+        centre_px towards the viewer (-Y) from the gun's middle."""
+        d = depth_px * K
+        c = -centre_px * K
+        return self.slab_from_curve(self.polygon_curve(pts), c - d / 2, c + d / 2)
+
+    def cyl_x(self, x0, x1, yc, r_px, verts=48, r1_px=None, depth_c=0.0, fill=True):
+        """A cylinder (or cone, r1) along X from reference x0 to x1 at height yc."""
+        n = self.node("GeometryNodeMeshCone")
+        n.inputs["Vertices"].default_value = verts
+        n.inputs["Radius Top"].default_value = (r1_px if r1_px is not None else r_px) * K
+        n.inputs["Radius Bottom"].default_value = r_px * K
+        n.inputs["Depth"].default_value = abs(x1 - x0) * K
+        if not fill:
+            n.fill_type = "NONE"
+        X0, Z = P(x0, yc)
+        X1, _ = P(x1, yc)
+        # (the cone runs from its base at 0 up +Z, which is turned to +X: base at x0)
+        return self.transform(n.outputs["Mesh"], loc=(X0, -depth_c * K, Z), rot=(0, math.pi / 2, 0))
+
+    def cyl_y(self, x, y, r_px, depth_px, front_px, verts=40):
+        """A short cylinder facing the viewer (axis Y) at reference (x, y); its
+        front face front_px towards the viewer from the gun's middle."""
+        n = self.node("GeometryNodeMeshCylinder")
+        n.inputs["Vertices"].default_value = verts
+        n.inputs["Radius"].default_value = r_px * K
+        n.inputs["Depth"].default_value = depth_px * K
+        X, Z = P(x, y)
+        return self.transform(n.outputs["Mesh"], loc=(X, -(front_px - depth_px / 2) * K, Z), rot=(math.pi / 2, 0, 0))
+
+    def box(self, x0, y0, x1, y1, depth_px, centre_px=0.0):
+        return self.slab([(x0, y0), (x1, y0), (x1, y1), (x0, y1)], depth_px, centre_px)
+
+    def sweep(self, curve, radius_m, res=10, caps=True):
+        prof = self.node("GeometryNodeCurvePrimitiveCircle")
+        prof.inputs["Resolution"].default_value = res
+        prof.inputs["Radius"].default_value = radius_m
+        m = self.node("GeometryNodeCurveToMesh")
+        self.link(curve, m.inputs["Curve"])
+        self.link(prof.outputs["Curve"], m.inputs["Profile Curve"])
+        m.inputs["Fill Caps"].default_value = caps
+        return m.outputs["Mesh"]
+
+    def path(self, pts, depth_front_px, resample=None):
+        """An open curve through reference pixels, at depth depth_front_px towards the viewer."""
+        line = self.node("GeometryNodeCurvePrimitiveLine")
+        rs = self.node("GeometryNodeResampleCurve")
+        self.link(line.outputs[0], rs.inputs["Curve"])
+        rs.inputs["Count"].default_value = len(pts)
+        sw = self.node("GeometryNodeIndexSwitch", data_type="VECTOR")
+        while len(sw.index_switch_items) < len(pts):
+            sw.index_switch_items.new()
+        self.link(self.node("GeometryNodeInputIndex").outputs[0], sw.inputs["Index"])
+        for i, (x, y) in enumerate(pts):
+            X, Z = P(x, y)
+            sw.inputs[str(i)].default_value = (X, -depth_front_px * K, Z)
+        sp = self.node("GeometryNodeSetPosition")
+        self.link(rs.outputs[0], sp.inputs["Geometry"])
+        self.link(sw.outputs[0], sp.inputs["Position"])
+        out = sp.outputs[0]
+        # smooth it: a Catmull-Rom-ish spline through the points
+        st = self.node("GeometryNodeCurveSplineType", spline_type="CATMULL_ROM")
+        self.link(out, st.inputs["Curve"])
+        out = st.outputs[0]
+        if resample:
+            rs2 = self.node("GeometryNodeResampleCurve")
+            self.link(out, rs2.inputs["Curve"])
+            rs2.inputs["Count"].default_value = resample
+            out = rs2.outputs[0]
+        return out
+
+    # --- distance fields ----------------------------------------------------------
+
+    def sdf(self, mesh, voxel):
+        n = self.node("GeometryNodeMeshToSDFGrid")
+        self.link(mesh, n.inputs["Mesh"])
+        n.inputs["Voxel Size"].default_value = voxel
+        n.inputs["Band Width"].default_value = 4
+        return n.outputs[0]
+
+    def offset(self, grid, d):
+        n = self.node("GeometryNodeSDFGridOffset")
+        self.link(grid, n.inputs["Grid"])
+        n.inputs["Distance"].default_value = d
+        return n.outputs[0]
+
+    def to_mesh(self, grid):
+        n = self.node("GeometryNodeGridToMesh")
+        self.link(grid, n.inputs["Grid"])
+        n.inputs["Threshold"].default_value = 0.0
+        return n.outputs[0]
+
+    def rounded(self, mesh, r, voxel):
+        """mesh with its edges rounded by r (eroded then grown back)."""
+        return self.to_mesh(self.offset(self.offset(self.sdf(mesh, voxel), r), -r))
+
+    def carve(self, mesh, cutters, voxel):
+        a = self.sdf(mesh, voxel)
+        n = self.node("GeometryNodeSDFGridBoolean", operation="DIFFERENCE")
+        self.link(a, n.inputs["Grid 1"])
+        for c in cutters:
+            self.link(self.sdf(c, voxel), n.inputs["Grid 2"])
+        return self.to_mesh(n.outputs[0])
+
+
+# --- materials ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def _principled(m):
+    m.use_nodes = True
+    return m.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
+
+
+def worn(name, base, metal, rough, rust=(0.6, 0.27, 0.07), chips=(0.045, 0.032, 0.028), rust_amt=0.45, chip_amt=0.28, scale=40.0, pits=1.0):
+    """Painted / bare metal, worn: rust patches (orange-brown) and dark chips,
+    from two noise textures; rust and chips are rough and not metallic."""
+    m = bpy.data.materials.get(name) or bpy.data.materials.new(name)
+    b = _principled(m)
+    nt = m.node_tree
+    for n in list(nt.nodes):
+        if n.type not in ("BSDF_PRINCIPLED", "OUTPUT_MATERIAL"):
+            nt.nodes.remove(n)
+    co = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexCoord")
+    n1 = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexNoise"); n1.inputs["Scale"].default_value = scale; n1.inputs["Detail"].default_value = 10.0
+    n1.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = 0.65
+    n2 = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexNoise"); n2.inputs["Scale"].default_value = scale * 3.2; n2.inputs["Detail"].default_value = 6.0
+    for n in (n1, n2):
+        nt.links.new(co.outputs["Object"], n.inputs["Vector"])
+    r1 = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeValToRGB")   # rust mask
+    r1.color_ramp.elements[0].position = 1.0 - rust_amt
+    r1.color_ramp.elements[1].position = 1.0 - rust_amt + 0.06
+    nt.links.new(n1.outputs["Fac"], r1.inputs["Fac"])
+    r2 = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeValToRGB")   # chips mask
+    r2.color_ramp.elements[0].position = 1.0 - chip_amt
+    r2.color_ramp.elements[1].position = 1.0 - chip_amt + 0.03
+    nt.links.new(n2.outputs["Fac"], r2.inputs["Fac"])
+
+    def mix(a, bcol, fac):
+        mx = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeMix"); mx.data_type = "RGBA"
+        A = [s for s in mx.inputs if s.name == "A" and s.type == "RGBA"][0]
+        B = [s for s in mx.inputs if s.name == "B" and s.type == "RGBA"][0]
+        if isinstance(a, tuple):
+            A.default_value = (*a, 1)
+        else:
+            nt.links.new(a, A)
+        B.default_value = (*bcol, 1)
+        nt.links.new(fac, mx.inputs["Factor"])
+        return [s for s in mx.outputs if s.name == "Result" and s.type == "RGBA"][0]
+    # pits: small dark spots all over (Voronoi cells' centres), like the reference's pitted paint
+    vo = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexVoronoi"); vo.inputs["Scale"].default_value = scale * 7.0
+    vo.inputs["Randomness"].default_value = 1.0
+    nt.links.new(co.outputs["Object"], vo.inputs["Vector"])
+    r3 = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeValToRGB")
+    r3.color_ramp.elements[0].position = 0.12 * pits
+    r3.color_ramp.elements[1].position = 0.12 * pits + 0.04
+    r3.color_ramp.elements[0].color = (1, 1, 1, 1)
+    r3.color_ramp.elements[1].color = (0, 0, 0, 1)

+    col = mix(col, chips, r2.outputs["Color"])

+    nt.links.new(col, b.inputs["Base Color"])
+    # metallic / roughness: bare where painted, rough where rusted or chipped
+    worn_mask = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeMath"); worn_mask.operation = "MAXIMUM"
+    nt.links.new(r1.outputs["Color"], worn_mask.inputs[0]); nt.links.new(r2.outputs["Color"], worn_mask.inputs[1])
+    pit_mask = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeMath"); pit_mask.operation = "MAXIMUM"
+    nt.links.new(worn_mask.outputs[0], pit_mask.inputs[0]); nt.links.new(r3.outputs["Color"], pit_mask.inputs[1])

+    met.inputs["To Min"].default_value = metal; met.inputs["To Max"].default_value = 0.0

+    nt.links.new(met.outputs["Result"], b.inputs["Metallic"])

+    ro.inputs["To Min"].default_value = rough; ro.inputs["To Max"].default_value = 0.85

+        c.name = "Aim"
+        c.target = gun
+    cam = bpy.data.objects.get("Camera")
+    if cam is None:
+        cam = bpy.data.objects.new("Camera", bpy.data.cameras.new("Camera"))
+        sc.collection.objects.link(cam)
+    cam.data.type = "ORTHO"
+    sc.camera = cam
+    # Glow around the lights (render only): the compositor's bloom.
+    ct = bpy.data.node_groups.get("GunComp") or bpy.data.node_groups.new("GunComp", "CompositorNodeTree")
+    ct.nodes.clear()
+    if not ct.interface.items_tree:
+        ct.interface.new_socket("Image", in_out="OUTPUT", socket_type="NodeSocketColor")
+    rl = ct.nodes.new("CompositorNodeRLayers")
+    gl = ct.nodes.new("CompositorNodeGlare")
+    gl.inputs["Type"].default_value = "Bloom"
+    gl.inputs["Threshold"].default_value = 2.5   # (only the glowing lights, not shiny metal)
+    gl.inputs["Strength"].default_value = 0.8
+    go = ct.nodes.new("NodeGroupOutput")
+    ct.links.new(rl.outputs["Image"], gl.inputs["Image"])
+    ct.links.new(gl.outputs["Image"], go.inputs[0])
+    sc.compositing_node_group = ct
+    return cam
+
+
+def render_views(cam):
+    sc = bpy.context.scene
+    views = (("side", -90, 0, 1.0), ("q3", -60, 20, 0.85), ("rear", 120, 15, 0.85), ("top", -90, 75, 1.0))
+    for name, az, el, sc_ in views:
+        a, e = math.radians(az), math.radians(el)
+        tgt = (0.0, 0.0, P(1000, 330)[1])
+        d = 3.0
+        cam.location = (tgt[0] + d * math.cos(e) * math.cos(a), tgt[1] + d * math.cos(e) * math.sin(a), tgt[2] + d * math.sin(e))
+        cam.rotation_euler = (math.pi / 2 - e, 0, a + math.pi / 2)
+        cam.data.ortho_scale = 2000 * K * sc_
+        sc.render.filepath = os.path.join(HERE, "preview_%s.png" % name)
+        bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
+
+
+def split_parts(src, name="AAD-73"):
+    """The gun as separate objects, one per part (from the "part" attribute the
+    node tree tags every piece with), each with its origin at its middle, all
+    in the collection `name` and parented to an empty `name` - move, turn or
+    scale that and the whole gun follows. The procedural object `src` stays in
+    the file, in a hidden collection "<name> (procedural)" - rebuild from it."""
+    import bmesh
+    from mathutils import Vector
+    sc = bpy.context.scene
+    col = bpy.data.collections.get(name) or bpy.data.collections.new(name)
+    if col.name not in sc.collection.children:
+        sc.collection.children.link(col)
+    for ob in list(col.objects):
+        bpy.data.objects.remove(ob)
+    root = bpy.data.objects.new(name, None)
+    root.empty_display_type = "PLAIN_AXES"
+    root.empty_display_size = 0.15
+    col.objects.link(root)
+    ev = src.evaluated_get(bpy.context.evaluated_depsgraph_get())
+    whole = bpy.data.meshes.new_from_object(ev)
+    made = []
+    for idx, pname in enumerate(PARTS):
+        bm = bmesh.new()
+        bm.from_mesh(whole)
+        lay = bm.faces.layers.int.get("part")
+        drop = [f for f in bm.faces if f[lay] != idx]
+        bmesh.ops.delete(bm, geom=drop, context="FACES")
+        loose = [v for v in bm.verts if not v.link_faces]
+        bmesh.ops.delete(bm, geom=loose, context="VERTS")
+        if not bm.faces:
+            bm.free()
+            continue
+        used = sorted({f.material_index for f in bm.faces})
+        remap = {m: i for i, m in enumerate(used)}
+        for f in bm.faces:
+            f.material_index = remap[f.material_index]
+        lo = Vector((min(v.co.x for v in bm.verts), min(v.co.y for v in bm.verts), min(v.co.z for v in bm.verts)))
+        hi = Vector((max(v.co.x for v in bm.verts), max(v.co.y for v in bm.verts), max(v.co.z for v in bm.verts)))
+        mid = (lo + hi) / 2
+        bmesh.ops.translate(bm, verts=bm.verts, vec=-mid)
+        me = bpy.data.meshes.new(pname)
+        bm.to_mesh(me)
+        bm.free()
+        for m in used:
+            me.materials.append(whole.materials[m])
+        if "part" in me.attributes:
+            me.attributes.remove(me.attributes["part"])
+        ob = bpy.data.objects.new(pname, me)
+        ob.location = mid
+        ob.parent = root
+        col.objects.link(ob)
+        made.append(ob)
+    bpy.data.meshes.remove(whole)
+    # The procedural source: out of the way, kept.
+    srcname = name + " (procedural)"
+    scol = bpy.data.collections.get(srcname) or bpy.data.collections.new(srcname)
+    if scol.name not in sc.collection.children:
+        sc.collection.children.link(scol)
+    for c in list(src.users_collection):
+        c.objects.unlink(src)
+    scol.objects.link(src)
+    lc = bpy.context.view_layer.layer_collection.children.get(srcname)
+    if lc:
+        lc.exclude = True
+    src.hide_render = True
+    return root, made
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    bpy.ops.wm.read_homefile(use_empty=True)
+    gun = build()
+    cam = stage()
+    os.makedirs(HERE, exist_ok=True)
+    bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=os.path.join(HERE, "gun2.blend"))
+    render_views(cam)
+    root, made = split_parts(gun)   # (after the renders: they use the procedural object)
+    print("split into", len(made), "objects:", ", ".join(o.name for o in made))
+    bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=os.path.join(HERE, "gun2.blend"))

@@ -1,0 +1,700 @@ 
+"""The pirate's tricorne, made entirely with geometry nodes (one node tree,
+"PirateHat", on the object "PirateHat" - an empty mesh; everything comes
+from the nodes).
+
+Reference: the pirate sprite (art/pirate/pirate_idle_s.png / _e.png): a dark
+red-brown hat - a rounded crown, the brim turned up into four walls that
+meet in four points at the corners, a gold trim
+with little gold spikes along the brim's edge, and a skull and crossbones on
+the front wall.
+
+How the nodes build it:
+  Brim   a Grid in (angle, across) space bent into a surface of revolution:
+         out from the crown (a ledge), then up into four walls (front, back,
+         left, right) that lean out a little; the outline is drawn out to four
+         corner points, which flick up; the front and back walls rise to a
+         peak in the middle (triangles), the back one a little higher. Extruded for thickness; the hat is a bit wider
+         than deep.
+  Crown  a UV sphere's top half, squashed and raised.
+  Trim   the brim's outer edge as a curve (same formula, across ~1) swept
+         with a small circle; gold balls on the points and gold hooks hanging
+         from the front two.
+  Slime  liquid-gold goo along the top edges: the edge curve swept with a lumpy
+         (noise) radius, and drips hanging from it - tapering stems and bulbs
+         instanced on random points, random lengths - all meshed together
+         through a filleted distance field so they flow into each other.
+  Skull  spheres, a cube and cylinders on the front wall (skull, jaw, eyes,
+         nose, two crossed bones).
+The shape's numbers are the constants below (re-run to rebuild).
+
+  blender -b --python external/blender/pirate_hat/build_hat.py      (or run in Blender)
+Saves external/blender/pirate_hat/pirate_hat.blend and preview renders.
+"""
+import math
+import os
+
+import bpy
+
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) if "__file__" in globals() else \
+    "/home/kilon/MEGA/Dimitris/godot/space-atrapos/external/blender/pirate_hat"
+
+# Shape (metres; the pirate is 0.96 m tall, its head about 0.14 m).
+R0 = 0.095          # the crown's radius, where the brim starts
+R_MID = 0.15        # the walls' middle, from the centre
+RC = 0.218          # ... the points
+POINTED = 1.6       # how sharply the outline draws out to a point
+H_FRONT = 0.085     # wall height: the front wall (at its corners' end)
+H_BACK = 0.1        # ... the back wall (rises over the crown, seen from the front)
+POINT_RISE = 0.03   # the corners flick up this much higher
+PEAK = 0.085        # the front and back walls rise this much to a peak in the middle (triangles)
+THICK = 0.008
+SKULL = 0.034       # the skull's width (m, before the emblem's 1.35 scale)
+SKULL_VOXEL = 0.018 # its SDF resolution (in skull widths): smaller = finer
+WIDEN = (1.14, 0.94, 1.0)   # the whole hat: wider than deep
+FLARE = 0.045       # how far the walls lean out at the top
+POINTS_AT = (45.0, 135.0, 225.0, 315.0)   # degrees: the four corners (front = -Y): front, back, left and right walls
+DRIPS = 64          # places along the edge a drip may hang from (about 40% do)
+DRIP_R = 0.0038     # m, a drip's radius where it leaves the edge
+SLIME_BAND = 0.006  # m, the goo along the edge (radius, plus up to as much again, lumpy)
+SLIME_VOXEL = 0.0016  # m, the slime's distance-field resolution
+SLIME = (0.95, 0.6, 0.1)   # the slime's colour: liquid gold
+
+LEATHER = (0.2, 0.026, 0.01)
+GOLD = (0.95, 0.62, 0.18)
+BONE = (0.85, 0.78, 0.62)
+
+
+# --- node helpers --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+class G:
+    def __init__(self, tree):
+        self.t = tree
+        self.x = 0
+
+    def node(self, kind, **props):
+        n = self.t.nodes.new(kind)
+        for k, v in props.items():
+            setattr(n, k, v)
+        n.location = (self.x, 0)
+        self.x += 40
+        return n
+
+    def link(self, a, b):
+        self.t.links.new(a, b)
+
+    def math(self, op, a, b=None, c=None):
+        n = self.node("ShaderNodeMath", operation=op)
+        for i, v in enumerate((a, b, c)):
+            if v is None:
+                continue
+            if isinstance(v, (int, float)):
+                n.inputs[i].default_value = v
+            else:
+                self.link(v, n.inputs[i])
+        return n.outputs[0]
+
+    def vmath(self, op, a, b=None):
+        n = self.node("ShaderNodeVectorMath", operation=op)
+        for i, v in enumerate((a, b)):
+            if v is None:
+                continue
+            if isinstance(v, (tuple, list)):
+                n.inputs[i].default_value = v
+            elif isinstance(v, (int, float)):
+                n.inputs[3].default_value = v   # (scale)
+            else:
+                self.link(v, n.inputs[i])
+        return n.outputs[0]
+
+    def combine(self, x, y, z):
+        n = self.node("ShaderNodeCombineXYZ")
+        for i, v in enumerate((x, y, z)):
+            if isinstance(v, (int, float)):
+                n.inputs[i].default_value = v
+            else:
+                self.link(v, n.inputs[i])
+        return n.outputs[0]
+
+    def separate(self, v):
+        n = self.node("ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ")
+        self.link(v, n.inputs[0])
+        return n.outputs[0], n.outputs[1], n.outputs[2]
+
+    def material(self, geo, mat):
+        n = self.node("GeometryNodeSetMaterial")
+        self.link(geo, n.inputs["Geometry"])
+        n.inputs["Material"].default_value = mat
+        return n.outputs[0]
+
+    def transform(self, geo, loc=(0, 0, 0), rot=(0, 0, 0), scale=(1, 1, 1)):
+        n = self.node("GeometryNodeTransform")
+        self.link(geo, n.inputs["Geometry"])
+        n.inputs["Translation"].default_value = loc
+        n.inputs["Rotation"].default_value = rot
+        n.inputs["Scale"].default_value = scale
+        return n.outputs[0]
+
+    def join(self, *geos):
+        n = self.node("GeometryNodeJoinGeometry")
+        for g in reversed(geos):   # (the multi-input socket stacks them)
+            self.link(g, n.inputs[0])
+        return n.outputs[0]
+
+    def smooth(self, geo):
+        n = self.node("GeometryNodeSetShadeSmooth")
+        self.link(geo, n.inputs["Geometry"])
+        return n.outputs[0]
+
+
+def brim_point(g, theta, across):
+    """The brim surface at (theta, across 0..1) - node sockets in, a position out."""
+    period = 2 * math.pi / len(POINTS_AT)
+    th0 = math.radians(POINTS_AT[0])
+    local = g.math("SUBTRACT", g.math("FLOORED_MODULO", g.math("SUBTRACT", theta, th0 - period / 2), period), period / 2)
+    u = g.math("DIVIDE", g.math("ABSOLUTE", local), period / 2)          # 0 at a point .. 1 mid-wall
+    pt = g.math("SUBTRACT", 1.0, u)
+    # The outline: the walls' middle R_MID out, drawn out to RC at the points.
+    ro = g.math("ADD", R_MID, g.math("MULTIPLY", g.math("POWER", pt, POINTED), RC - R_MID))
+    near = g.math("POWER", pt, 3.0)
+    # Wall height: the front wall a little lower (the face and skull show), the
+    # back wall rising behind the crown; the points flick up higher still.
+    sn = g.math("SINE", theta)                                    # -1 front .. 1 back
+    x = g.math("MINIMUM", g.math("MAXIMUM", g.math("DIVIDE", g.math("ADD", sn, 0.35), 0.7), 0.0), 1.0)
+    t = g.math("MULTIPLY", g.math("MULTIPLY", x, x), g.math("SUBTRACT", 3.0, g.math("MULTIPLY", x, 2.0)))   # (smoothstep)
+    h = g.math("ADD", H_FRONT, g.math("MULTIPLY", t, H_BACK - H_FRONT))
+    # (the front points flick up; the back one less, keeping the top line level)
+    rise = g.math("MULTIPLY", g.math("SUBTRACT", 1.0, g.math("MULTIPLY", g.math("MAXIMUM", sn, 0.0), 0.75)), POINT_RISE)
+    h = g.math("ADD", h, g.math("MULTIPLY", near, rise))
+    # The front and back walls rise to a peak in the middle - a triangle - (straight
+    # edges: linear in x = r cos(theta)); the side walls don't.
+    tri = g.math("MAXIMUM", g.math("SUBTRACT", 1.0, g.math("DIVIDE", g.math("ABSOLUTE", g.math("COSINE", theta)), 0.7071)), 0.0)
+    h = g.math("ADD", h, g.math("MULTIPLY", tri, PEAK))
+    # Profile: out from the crown, then turning up into a wall.
+    # (out first - a ledge - then up: the walls stand nearly upright)
+    q = g.math("MULTIPLY", g.math("MINIMUM", g.math("DIVIDE", across, 0.62), 1.0), math.pi / 2)
+    q2 = g.math("MULTIPLY", g.math("MAXIMUM", g.math("DIVIDE", g.math("SUBTRACT", across, 0.3), 0.7), 0.0), math.pi / 2)
+    rad = g.math("ADD", R0, g.math("MULTIPLY", g.math("SUBTRACT", ro, R0), g.math("SINE", q)))
+    rad = g.math("ADD", rad, g.math("MULTIPLY", g.math("SINE", q2), FLARE))   # (the walls lean out)
+    z = g.math("MULTIPLY", h, g.math("SUBTRACT", 1.0, g.math("COSINE", q2)))
+    # The walls lean out a little more at the points, which droop slightly.
+    z = g.math("SUBTRACT", z, g.math("MULTIPLY", g.math("MULTIPLY", near, across), 0.012))
+    x = g.math("MULTIPLY", rad, g.math("COSINE", theta))
+    y = g.math("MULTIPLY", rad, g.math("SINE", theta))
+    return g.combine(x, y, z), (rad, z, near)
+
+
+def build():
+    # Materials.
+    def mat(name, col, metal=0.0, rough=0.6):
+        m = bpy.data.materials.get(name) or bpy.data.materials.new(name)
+        m.use_nodes = True
+        b = m.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
+        b.inputs["Base Color"].default_value = (*col, 1)
+        b.inputs["Metallic"].default_value = metal
+        b.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = rough
+        b.inputs["Specular IOR Level"].default_value = 0.35 if metal == 0.0 else 0.5
+        if name == "HatBone":   # (old bone: ivory to yellowed, darker in the crevices)
+            nt = m.node_tree
+            nz = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexNoise"); nz.inputs["Scale"].default_value = 60.0; nz.inputs["Detail"].default_value = 8.0
+            ramp = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeValToRGB")
+            ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].color = (0.45, 0.36, 0.22, 1)
+            ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].color = (0.8, 0.74, 0.6, 1)
+            nt.links.new(nz.outputs["Fac"], ramp.inputs["Fac"])
+            ao = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeAmbientOcclusion"); ao.inputs["Distance"].default_value = 0.004
+            mul = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeMix"); mul.data_type = "RGBA"; mul.blend_type = "MULTIPLY"
+            mul.inputs["Factor"].default_value = 0.85
+            col = lambda socks, nm: [x for x in socks if x.name == nm and x.type == "RGBA"][0]   # (the Mix node's colour sockets)
+            nt.links.new(ramp.outputs["Color"], col(mul.inputs, "A"))
+            nt.links.new(ao.outputs["AO"], col(mul.inputs, "B"))   # (AO as a grey: dark in the hollows)
+            nt.links.new(col(mul.outputs, "Result"), b.inputs["Base Color"])
+            bm = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeBump"); bm.inputs["Strength"].default_value = 0.15
+            nt.links.new(nz.outputs["Fac"], bm.inputs["Height"]); nt.links.new(bm.outputs["Normal"], b.inputs["Normal"])
+        if name == "HatLeather":   # (worn leather: a little bump)
+            nt = m.node_tree
+            nz = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexNoise"); nz.inputs["Scale"].default_value = 90.0; nz.inputs["Detail"].default_value = 6.0
+            bm = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeBump"); bm.inputs["Strength"].default_value = 0.25
+            nt.links.new(nz.outputs["Fac"], bm.inputs["Height"]); nt.links.new(bm.outputs["Normal"], b.inputs["Normal"])
+        return m
+    m_leather = mat("HatLeather", LEATHER, 0.0, 0.75)
+    m_gold = mat("HatGold", GOLD, 1.0, 0.32)
+    m_bone = mat("HatBone", BONE, 0.0, 0.5)
+    m_dark = mat("HatSocket", (0.03, 0.02, 0.02), 0.0, 0.8)
+    m_slime = mat("HatSlime", SLIME, 0.55, 0.12)   # (molten-gold goo: wet, half metallic, a faint glow)
+    bs = m_slime.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
+    bs.inputs["Transmission Weight"].default_value = 0.1
+    bs.inputs["Emission Color"].default_value = (*SLIME, 1)
+    bs.inputs["Emission Strength"].default_value = 0.25
+    bs.inputs["Coat Weight"].default_value = 0.6
+    bs.inputs["Subsurface Weight"].default_value = 0.3
+
+    tree = bpy.data.node_groups.get("PirateHat")
+    if tree:
+        bpy.data.node_groups.remove(tree)
+    tree = bpy.data.node_groups.new("PirateHat", "GeometryNodeTree")
+    tree.interface.new_socket("Geometry", in_out="OUTPUT", socket_type="NodeSocketGeometry")
+    g = G(tree)
+    out = g.node("NodeGroupOutput")
+
+    # --- Brim: a grid in (angle, across) space -------------------------------------------
+    grid = g.node("GeometryNodeMeshGrid")
+    grid.inputs["Size X"].default_value = 2 * math.pi
+    grid.inputs["Size Y"].default_value = 1.0
+    grid.inputs["Vertices X"].default_value = 241
+    grid.inputs["Vertices Y"].default_value = 14
+    pos = g.node("GeometryNodeInputPosition").outputs[0]
+    gx, gy, _ = g.separate(pos)
+    theta = g.math("ADD", gx, math.pi)
+    across = g.math("ADD", gy, 0.5)
+    p, _ = brim_point(g, theta, across)
+    setp = g.node("GeometryNodeSetPosition")
+    g.link(grid.outputs["Mesh"], setp.inputs["Geometry"])
+    g.link(p, setp.inputs["Position"])
+    weld = g.node("GeometryNodeMergeByDistance")   # (the seam at 0 / 360 deg)
+    g.link(setp.outputs[0], weld.inputs["Geometry"])
+    weld.inputs["Distance"].default_value = 0.0005
+    ext = g.node("GeometryNodeExtrudeMesh")        # thickness
+    g.link(weld.outputs[0], ext.inputs["Mesh"])
+    ext.inputs["Offset Scale"].default_value = THICK
+    ext.inputs["Individual"].default_value = False
+    brim = g.material(g.smooth(ext.outputs["Mesh"]), m_leather)
+
+    # --- Crown: a squashed dome with a dent along the top --------------------------------
+    sph = g.node("GeometryNodeMeshUVSphere")
+    sph.inputs["Segments"].default_value = 64
+    sph.inputs["Rings"].default_value = 32
+    sph.inputs["Radius"].default_value = 1.0
+    pos2 = g.node("GeometryNodeInputPosition").outputs[0]
+    sx, sy, sz = g.separate(pos2)
+    zc = g.math("MAXIMUM", sz, -0.25)
+    dent = g.math("MULTIPLY", g.math("MULTIPLY", g.math("POWER", g.math("MAXIMUM", zc, 0.0), 3.0),
+                                     g.math("EXPONENT", g.math("MULTIPLY", g.math("MULTIPLY", sx, sx), -18.0))), 0.03)
+    cp = g.combine(g.math("MULTIPLY", sx, R0 * 1.06), g.math("MULTIPLY", sy, R0 * 0.98),
+                   g.math("MULTIPLY", g.math("SUBTRACT", zc, dent), 0.165))
+    setc = g.node("GeometryNodeSetPosition")
+    g.link(sph.outputs["Mesh"], setc.inputs["Geometry"])
+    g.link(cp, setc.inputs["Position"])
+    crown = g.material(g.smooth(g.transform(setc.outputs[0], loc=(0, 0, 0.035), scale=(1.08, 1.08, 1.0))), m_leather)
+    # A band round the crown's foot.
+    band = g.node("GeometryNodeMeshCylinder")
+    band.inputs["Vertices"].default_value = 64
+    band.inputs["Radius"].default_value = R0 * 1.075
+    band.inputs["Depth"].default_value = 0.016
+    band_g = g.material(g.smooth(g.transform(band.outputs["Mesh"], loc=(0, 0, 0.014), scale=(1.06, 0.98, 1))),
+                        bpy.data.materials["HatSocket"])
+
+    # --- Gold trim: the brim's outer edge, swept with a little circle --------------------
+    circ = g.node("GeometryNodeCurvePrimitiveCircle")
+    circ.inputs["Resolution"].default_value = 240
+    circ.inputs["Radius"].default_value = 1.0
+    pos3 = g.node("GeometryNodeInputPosition").outputs[0]
+    cx, cy, _ = g.separate(pos3)
+    th3 = g.math("ARCTAN2", cy, cx)
+    p3, _ = brim_point(g, th3, 0.985)
+    sett = g.node("GeometryNodeSetPosition")
+    g.link(circ.outputs["Curve"], sett.inputs["Geometry"])
+    g.link(p3, sett.inputs["Position"])
+    prof = g.node("GeometryNodeCurvePrimitiveCircle")
+    prof.inputs["Resolution"].default_value = 8
+    prof.inputs["Radius"].default_value = 0.0065

+def skull_unit(g, m_bone, m_dark):
+    """A human skull one unit wide, facing -Y, centred on the origin: bone
+    shapes (cranium, brow, cheekbones, upper jaw, lower jaw, chin) as signed
+    distance fields joined smoothly, the eye sockets, nose cavity and the gap
+    between the jaws carved out, then meshed; teeth along both jaws, and
+    shadowy dark hollows deep in the sockets and the nose."""
+    def ellipsoid(c, r, rot=(0, 0, 0)):
+        sp = g.node("GeometryNodeMeshUVSphere")
+        sp.inputs["Segments"].default_value = 32
+        sp.inputs["Rings"].default_value = 16
+        sp.inputs["Radius"].default_value = 1.0
+        return g.transform(sp.outputs["Mesh"], loc=c, rot=rot, scale=r)
+
+    def box(c, size, rot=(0, 0, 0)):
+        cb = g.node("GeometryNodeMeshCube")
+        cb.inputs["Size"].default_value = size
+        return g.transform(cb.outputs["Mesh"], loc=c, rot=rot)
+
+    def sdf(mesh):
+        n = g.node("GeometryNodeMeshToSDFGrid")
+        g.link(mesh, n.inputs["Mesh"])
+        n.inputs["Voxel Size"].default_value = SKULL_VOXEL
+        n.inputs["Band Width"].default_value = 4
+        return n.outputs[0]
+
+    def boolean(op, a, bs):
+        n = g.node("GeometryNodeSDFGridBoolean", operation=op)
+        if a is not None:
+            g.link(a, n.inputs["Grid 1"])
+        for b in reversed(bs):
+            g.link(b, n.inputs["Grid 2"])
+        return n.outputs[0]
+
+    bone = [

+        ellipsoid((0, -0.3, 0.1), (0.4, 0.2, 0.17)),            # the brow ridge

+def _outline(th, across):
+    """brim_point's radius and height in plain Python (to place things on the brim)."""
+    period = 2 * math.pi / len(POINTS_AT)
+    th0 = math.radians(POINTS_AT[0])
+    local = ((th - (th0 - period / 2)) % period) - period / 2
+    pt = 1.0 - abs(local) / (period / 2)
+    ro = R_MID + (pt ** POINTED) * (RC - R_MID)
+    near = pt ** 3
+    sn = math.sin(th)
+    x = min(max((sn + 0.35) / 0.7, 0.0), 1.0)
+    h = H_FRONT + x * x * (3 - 2 * x) * (H_BACK - H_FRONT) + near * POINT_RISE * (1 - 0.75 * max(sn, 0.0))
+    h += max(0.0, 1 - abs(math.cos(th)) / 0.7071) * PEAK
+    q = min(across / 0.62, 1.0) * math.pi / 2
+    q2 = max((across - 0.3) / 0.7, 0.0) * math.pi / 2
+    rad = R0 + (ro - R0) * math.sin(q) + math.sin(q2) * FLARE
+    z = h * (1 - math.cos(q2)) - near * across * 0.012
+    return rad, z
+

+        cam.location = (tgt[0] + d * math.cos(e) * math.cos(a), tgt[1] + d * math.cos(e) * math.sin(a), tgt[2] + d * math.sin(e))
+        cam.rotation_euler = (math.pi / 2 - e, 0, a + math.pi / 2)
+        sc.render.filepath = os.path.join(HERE, "%s_%s.png" % (prefix, name))
+        bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
+        out.append(sc.render.filepath)
+    return out
+
+
+def render_skull(cam):
+    """A close-up of the skull, straight on (preview_skull.png)."""
+    sc = bpy.context.scene
+    rr, zz = _outline(-math.pi / 2, 0.88)
+    cam.location = (0, -3.0, zz + 0.003)
+    cam.rotation_euler = (math.pi / 2, 0, 0)
+    old = cam.data.ortho_scale
+    cam.data.ortho_scale = 0.09
+    sc.render.filepath = os.path.join(HERE, "preview_skull.png")
+    bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
+    cam.data.ortho_scale = old
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    bpy.ops.wm.read_homefile(use_empty=True)   # (a new, empty file)
+    ob = build()
+    cam = stage()
+    bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=os.path.join(HERE, "pirate_hat.blend"))
+    render_views(cam)
+    render_skull(cam)

files.explanation: New: FogOfWar - a grid of how well each patch of a map has been seen, revealed in soft circles, drawn as a smoothed dark texture, saved compactly. Used by the planet surfaces and the star systems.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,109 @@ 
+class_name FogOfWar
+extends RefCounted
+## Fog of war for a map: a grid of how well each patch has been seen (0
+## never .. 255 seen), revealed in soft-edged circles around you, saved as
+## base64. The planet surfaces (PlanetSurface.fog: one cell per 4 tiles,
+## grid coordinates) and the star systems (Galaxy.fog: one cell per CELL
+## world units round the star) use it; the maps draw texture() over what
+## they show - dark where you haven't been - and hide what lies in the dark.
+
+## Seen at least this much: explored (its things show on the maps).
+const SEEN := 110
+
+var cols := 0
+var rows := 0
+var origin := Vector2.ZERO          # the grid's corner, in the map's own coordinates
+var cell := 1.0                     # one cell's size, in the same units
+var data := PackedByteArray()
+var _image: Image
+var _texture: ImageTexture
+var _dirty := true
+## How dark the unexplored parts are drawn (alpha).
+var shade := 0.93
+## The texture is this many texels per cell, smoothed (soft edges even where
+## the map draws without filtering).
+var smooth := 4
+
+
+func _init(cols_: int, rows_: int, origin_ := Vector2.ZERO, cell_ := 1.0) -> void:
+	cols = cols_
+	rows = rows_
+	origin = origin_
+	cell = cell_
+	data.resize(cols * rows)
+
+
+## Reveals a circle (radius r, map units) round p; true if anything new was seen.
+func reveal(p: Vector2, r: float) -> bool:
+	var g := (p - origin) / cell
+	var rc := r / cell
+	var soft := maxf(rc * 0.3, 1.0)
+	var changed := false
+	for y in range(maxi(0, floori(g.y - rc)), mini(rows, ceili(g.y + rc) + 1)):
+		for x in range(maxi(0, floori(g.x - rc)), mini(cols, ceili(g.x + rc) + 1)):
+			var d := Vector2(x + 0.5, y + 0.5).distance_to(g)
+			if d > rc:
+				continue
+			var v := int(clampf((rc - d) / soft, 0.0, 1.0) * 255.0)
+			var i := y * cols + x
+			if v > data[i]:
+				data[i] = v
+				changed = true
+	if changed:
+		_dirty = true
+	return changed
+
+
+## How well the patch at p has been seen (0..255; outside the grid: 0).
+func seen_at(p: Vector2) -> int:
+	var g := (p - origin) / cell
+	var x := floori(g.x)
+	var y := floori(g.y)
+	if x < 0 or y < 0 or x >= cols or y >= rows:
+		return 0
+	return data[y * cols + x]
+
+
+func explored(p: Vector2) -> bool:
+	return seen_at(p) >= SEEN
+
+
+## Share of the map explored (0..1).
+func explored_share() -> float:
+	var n := 0
+	for v in data:
+		if v >= SEEN:
+			n += 1
+	return float(n) / maxf(data.size(), 1)
+
+
+## The fog to draw over the map (covering cols x rows cells): black,
+## transparent where seen, smoothed.
+func texture() -> ImageTexture:
+	if _dirty or _texture == null:
+		var la := PackedByteArray()
+		la.resize(cols * rows * 2)
+		for i in data.size():
+			la[i * 2 + 1] = int((255 - data[i]) * shade)
+		_image = Image.create_from_data(cols, rows, false, Image.FORMAT_LA8, la)
+		if smooth > 1:
+			_image.resize(cols * smooth, rows * smooth, Image.INTERPOLATE_BILINEAR)
+		if _texture == null or _texture.get_size() != Vector2(_image.get_size()):
+			_texture = ImageTexture.create_from_image(_image)
+		else:
+			_texture.update(_image)
+		_dirty = false
+	return _texture
+
+
+func save() -> String:
+	return Marshalls.raw_to_base64(data.compress(FileAccess.COMPRESSION_DEFLATE))
+
+
+func load_from(s: String) -> void:
+	if s == "":
+		return
+	var raw := Marshalls.base64_to_raw(s).decompress(cols * rows, FileAccess.COMPRESSION_DEFLATE)
+	if raw.size() == cols * rows:
+		data = raw
+		_dirty = true
hunks.title: FogOfWar
hunks.note: One byte per cell (0 never seen .. 255 seen); explored at 110; maps draw texture() over what they show.

bubbles.text: Explored once a cell is well past half-seen - the soft rim of a reveal doesn't count yet.
The outer 30 % of the circle fades out, so revealed areas have soft edges.
Only ever brighter: walking back through an explored patch never darkens it.
Luminance-alpha bytes: black, with alpha = how unseen (x0.93, so the dark still shows a hint of the map).
Upscaled 4x with smoothing on the CPU, so edges stay soft even on maps drawn without texture filtering.
A 220 x 220 grid is 48 KB raw; mostly 0 or 255, it deflates to a few hundred bytes in the save.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,374 @@ 
+class_name Furniture
+extends SurfaceProps.Thing
+## Furniture inside the Minoan buildings, drawn procedurally as isometric
+## boxes (no art files): standing against a room's back wall (the north-west
+## or north-east one, so it never hides you), facing into the room.
+##
+## Decoration:  table (a table and two chairs), chair, closet, bookshelf (a
+##              library shelf; scroll racks in temples), pithos (a tall Minoan
+##              storage jar), crates
+## Containers:  chest, locker, vault - click one: you walk up, open it and take
+##              what's inside (once; PlanetSurface.open_container keeps track).
+##
+## Geometry: a piece lives in one floor cell; its footprint is given in the
+## cell's grid units (di, dj in -0.5..0.5 around the cell's centre; +i is
+## down-right on screen, +j down-left). A piece against the "nw" wall has its
+## back on di = -0.5 and faces +i; against "ne", its back on dj = -0.5, facing
+## +j. The node sits at the footprint's centre (for y-sorting); `footprint`
+## (world polygon) blocks walking.
+
+const I := Vector2(64, 32)          # one cell along +i (world px)
+const J := Vector2(-64, 32)         # one cell along +j
+const CONTAINERS := ["chest", "locker", "vault"]
+const NAMES := {"table": "Table", "chair": "Chair", "closet": "Closet", "bookshelf": "Bookshelf",
+	"pithos": "Storage jar", "crates": "Crates", "chest": "Chest", "locker": "Lockers", "vault": "Vault"}
+## Sizes: [width along the wall, depth into the room, height px].
+const SIZE := {"table": [0.62, 0.72, 48.0], "chair": [0.34, 0.34, 62.0], "closet": [0.58, 0.24, 88.0],
+	"bookshelf": [0.74, 0.22, 94.0], "pithos": [0.36, 0.36, 50.0], "crates": [0.6, 0.4, 46.0],
+	"chest": [0.44, 0.28, 24.0], "locker": [0.74, 0.25, 86.0], "vault": [0.48, 0.42, 60.0]}
+const WOOD := Color(0.47, 0.29, 0.15)
+const DARK_WOOD := Color(0.32, 0.19, 0.1)
+const BRONZE := Color(0.83, 0.62, 0.3)
+const METAL := Color(0.5, 0.55, 0.6)
+const STEEL := Color(0.33, 0.36, 0.42)
+const CLAY := Color(0.72, 0.42, 0.24)
+const MINOAN_RED := Color(0.66, 0.18, 0.12)
+## The Minoan armchair (external/images/minoan_chair_sheet.png, cut by
+## tools/cut_soft_sheet.py; drawn at half its size, CHAIR_H tall: about 0.9 m
+## by the characters' 122 px / 1.8 m), by the way it faces.
+const CHAIR := {"se": preload("res://art/furniture/chair_se.png"), "sw": preload("res://art/furniture/chair_sw.png"),
+	"ne": preload("res://art/furniture/chair_ne.png"), "nw": preload("res://art/furniture/chair_nw.png")}
+const CHAIR_H := 62.0
+const TABLE_H := 48.0
+const BOOKS := [Color(0.62, 0.16, 0.12), Color(0.15, 0.32, 0.55), Color(0.78, 0.6, 0.22), Color(0.2, 0.42, 0.25),
+	Color(0.45, 0.22, 0.42), Color(0.85, 0.8, 0.65)]
+
+var kind := "chest"
+var wall := "nw"                    # the wall it stands against: "nw" or "ne"
+var style := "palace"               # the building's style (palace / warehouse / temple)
+var cell := Vector2i.ZERO
+var key := ""                       # for containers: "<i>,<j>" (opened ones stay opened)
+var opened := false
+var footprint := PackedVector2Array()   # world polygon (blocks walking)
+var seed_ := 0
+var _cell_c := Vector2.ZERO         # the cell's centre (world)
+var _fp := [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]     # di0, di1, dj0, dj1
+
+
+## Places it in `cell` (centre `c`, world) against `wall_`.
+func setup(kind_: String, wall_: String, cell_: Vector2i, c: Vector2, style_ := "palace") -> Furniture:
+	kind = kind_
+	wall = wall_
+	cell = cell_
+	style = style_
+	_cell_c = c
+	key = "%d,%d" % [cell.x, cell.y]
+	seed_ = hash(key + kind)
+	texture_filter = CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR_WITH_MIPMAPS   # (the chair's picture, shrunk)
+	var s: Array = SIZE[kind]
+	var w: float = s[0]
+	var d: float = s[1]
+	var gap := 0.06
+	if wall == "nw":
+		_fp = [-0.5 + gap, -0.5 + gap + d, -w / 2.0, w / 2.0]
+	else:
+		_fp = [-w / 2.0, w / 2.0, -0.5 + gap, -0.5 + gap + d]
+	var mid := Vector2((_fp[0] + _fp[1]) / 2.0, (_fp[2] + _fp[3]) / 2.0)
+	position = c + I * mid.x + J * mid.y
+	footprint = PackedVector2Array([_w(_fp[0], _fp[2]), _w(_fp[1], _fp[2]), _w(_fp[1], _fp[3]), _w(_fp[0], _fp[3])])
+	height = s[2]
+	click_radius = clampf(s[2] * 0.45 + 18.0, 28.0, 48.0)
+	_update_title()
+	return self
+
+
+func is_container() -> bool:
+	return kind in CONTAINERS
+
+
+func _update_title() -> void:
+	var n: String = NAMES[kind]
+	if kind == "bookshelf" and style == "temple":
+		n = "Scroll rack"
+	if is_container():
+		title = "%s  -  %s" % [n, "empty" if opened else "click to open"]
+	else:
+		title = n
+
+
+## Where you stand to open it: in front of it.
+func approach() -> Vector2:
+	var front := (I if wall == "nw" else J).normalized()
+	return position + front * (SIZE[kind][1] * 70.0 + 46.0)
+
+
+func click_center() -> Vector2:
+	return global_position + Vector2(0, -height * 0.5)
+
+
+func interact(surface: Node) -> void:
+	if is_container() and surface.has_method("open_container"):
+		surface.open_container(self)
+
+
+func set_opened(v: bool) -> void:
+	opened = v
+	_update_title()
+	queue_redraw()
+
+
+# --- Drawing ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+## World point of grid offset (di, dj) in the cell, at height h.
+func _w(di: float, dj: float, h := 0.0) -> Vector2:
+	return _cell_c + I * di + J * dj - Vector2(0, h)
+
+
+## Local (node) point.
+func _p(di: float, dj: float, h := 0.0) -> Vector2:
+	return _w(di, dj, h) - position
+
+
+## An isometric box: the top and the two faces you see (+i, +j).
+func _box(di0: float, di1: float, dj0: float, dj1: float, h0: float, h1: float, col: Color, outline := true) -> void:
+	var top := PackedVector2Array([_p(di0, dj0, h1), _p(di1, dj0, h1), _p(di1, dj1, h1), _p(di0, dj1, h1)])
+	var fi := PackedVector2Array([_p(di1, dj0, h0), _p(di1, dj1, h0), _p(di1, dj1, h1), _p(di1, dj0, h1)])   # +i face (down-right)
+	var fj := PackedVector2Array([_p(di0, dj1, h0), _p(di1, dj1, h0), _p(di1, dj1, h1), _p(di0, dj1, h1)])   # +j face (down-left)
+	if h1 - h0 > 0.5:
+		draw_colored_polygon(fi, col.darkened(0.28))
+		draw_colored_polygon(fj, col.darkened(0.08))
+	draw_colored_polygon(top, col.lightened(0.14))
+	if outline:
+		var o := Color(0.06, 0.04, 0.03, 0.55)
+		for poly in ([top, fi, fj] if h1 - h0 > 0.5 else [top]):
+			draw_polyline(poly + PackedVector2Array([poly[0]]), o, 1.0, true)
+
+
+## A point on the front face of the box (di0..dj1, h0..h1): s 0..1 left to
+## right as you look at it, t 0..1 bottom to top, pushed `out` a little.
+func _face(b: Array, s: float, t: float, out := 0.004) -> Vector2:
+	var h: float = lerpf(b[4], b[5], t)
+	if wall == "nw":   # front = the +i face; left to right on screen = dj high -> low
+		return _p(b[1] + out, lerpf(b[3], b[2], s), h)
+	return _p(lerpf(b[0], b[1], s), b[3] + out, h)   # front = the +j face; left to right = di low -> high
+
+
+func _face_quad(b: Array, s0: float, s1: float, t0: float, t1: float, col: Color, out := 0.004) -> void:
+	draw_colored_polygon(PackedVector2Array([_face(b, s0, t0, out), _face(b, s1, t0, out), _face(b, s1, t1, out), _face(b, s0, t1, out)]), col)
+
+
+func _face_line(b: Array, s0: float, t0: float, s1: float, t1: float, col: Color, w := 1.2) -> void:
+	draw_line(_face(b, s0, t0, 0.006), _face(b, s1, t1, 0.006), col, w, true)
+
+
+## The main box covering the footprint, from h0 to h1.
+func _main(h0: float, h1: float) -> Array:
+	return [_fp[0], _fp[1], _fp[2], _fp[3], h0, h1]
+
+
+func _draw() -> void:
+	SurfaceProps.shadow(self, 26.0 * SIZE[kind][0] / 0.5, 9.0, 0.22)
+	match kind:
+		"table": _draw_table()
+		"chair": _draw_chair(_fp, 1.0)
+		"closet": _draw_closet()
+		"bookshelf": _draw_bookshelf()
+		"pithos": _draw_pithos()
+		"crates": _draw_crates()
+		"chest": _draw_chest()
+		"locker": _draw_locker()
+		"vault": _draw_vault()
+
+
+func _draw_table() -> void:

files.explanation: New autoload Music: the scene's track (menu, space or surface), crossfading between two players, playing through pauses.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,117 @@ 
+extends Node
+## Autoload "Music": the background music. Three looping tracks in res://music/
+## (made by tools/music_gen.py, each a seamless 2-minute loop):
+##   menu     "Atrapos"        - the main menu and Talos (the editor)
+##   space    "Deep Drift"     - flying in space
+##   surface  "Minoan Shores"  - on a planet's surface (and the Library)
+## The track follows the scene by itself (TRACK_FOR: scene file -> track);
+## a change crossfades over FADE seconds. play("space") / stop() by hand too.
+## It plays on the "Music" bus, whose volume is Settings.music_volume; it keeps
+## playing while the game is paused (the menu over the game).
+
+const DIR := "res://music/"
+const BUS := "Music"
+const FADE := 2.5
+const TRACK_FOR := {
+	"res://loading.tscn": "menu",
+	"res://main_menu.tscn": "menu",
+	"res://editor.tscn": "menu",
+	"res://anim_editor.tscn": "menu",
+	"res://scenario_editor.tscn": "menu",
+	"res://svg_editor.tscn": "menu",
+	"res://patcher.tscn": "menu",
+	"res://main.tscn": "space",
+	"res://scenes/planet_surface.tscn": "surface",
+	"res://zoo.tscn": "surface",
+}
+const TITLES := {"menu": "Atrapos", "space": "Deep Drift", "surface": "Minoan Shores"}
+
+var current := ""                   # the track playing ("" none)
+var auto := true                    # follow the scene
+var _players: Array[AudioStreamPlayer] = []
+var _active := 0
+var _scene: Node
+var _tween: Tween
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS
+	if AudioServer.get_bus_index(BUS) < 0:
+		AudioServer.add_bus()
+		var i := AudioServer.bus_count - 1
+		AudioServer.set_bus_name(i, BUS)
+		AudioServer.set_bus_send(i, "Master")
+	for k in 2:
+		var p := AudioStreamPlayer.new()
+		p.bus = BUS
+		p.volume_db = -80.0
+		p.process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS
+		add_child(p)
+		_players.append(p)
+	apply_volume()
+
+
+## The Music bus at Settings.music_volume (0 = silent).
+func apply_volume() -> void:
+	var i := AudioServer.get_bus_index(BUS)
+	if i < 0:
+		return
+	var v: float = Settings.music_volume
+	AudioServer.set_bus_mute(i, v <= 0.001)
+	AudioServer.set_bus_volume_db(i, linear_to_db(maxf(v, 0.001)))
+
+
+## The track for a scene file ("" if none).
+func track_for(scene_path: String) -> String:
+	return TRACK_FOR.get(scene_path, "")
+
+
+func stream(track: String) -> AudioStream:
+	var path := "%s%s.ogg" % [DIR, track]
+	if not ResourceLoader.exists(path):
+		return null
+	var s: AudioStream = load(path)
+	if s is AudioStreamOggVorbis:
+		s.loop = true
+	return s
+
+
+## Crossfades to `track` (no change if it's already playing).
+func play(track: String, fade := FADE) -> void:
+	if track == current:
+		return
+	var s := stream(track) if track != "" else null
+	if track != "" and s == null:
+		return
+	current = track
+	var old := _players[_active]
+	_active = 1 - _active
+	var new := _players[_active]
+	if _tween:
+		_tween.kill()
+	_tween = create_tween().set_parallel(true)
+	_tween.set_pause_mode(Tween.TWEEN_PAUSE_PROCESS)
+	if s:
+		new.stream = s
+		new.volume_db = -60.0
+		new.play()
+		_tween.tween_property(new, "volume_db", 0.0, fade).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_SINE).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)
+	if old.playing:
+		_tween.tween_property(old, "volume_db", -60.0, fade).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_SINE).set_ease(Tween.EASE_IN)
+		_tween.chain().tween_callback(old.stop)
+
+
+func stop(fade := FADE) -> void:
+	play("", fade)
+
+
+func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
+	if not auto:
+		return
+	var sc := get_tree().current_scene
+	if sc == _scene or sc == null:
+		return
+	_scene = sc
+	var t := track_for(sc.scene_file_path)
+	if t != "":
+		play(t)

hunks.note: TRACK_FOR maps scene files to tracks; _process notices a new scene and crossfades over 2.5 s.

@@ -1,0 +1,146 @@ 
+extends Node
+## Autoload "Sfx": sound effects. Sounds live in res://sounds/<group>/ as
+## takes <name>_1.ogg, <name>_2.ogg ... (tools/sfx_pirate.py makes the
+## pirate's); a sound is called by "<group>/<name>" and each time one of its
+## takes plays, at a slightly random pitch, so repeats don't sound the same.
+##
+##   Sfx.play_at("pirate/shot", where, parent)   # in the world: fades with distance from the camera
+##   Sfx.play("pirate/loot_take")                # flat (for you: picking things up, the UI)
+##   Sfx.play_world("space/boom_big", global_pos) # at a global point, in the FX layer / scene
+##   var hum := Sfx.loop_at("space/station_hum", station)   # a looping sound on a node (yours to stop)
+##
+## Everything goes through the "SFX" bus, whose volume is Settings.sfx_volume.
+## A sound can't stack up endlessly: at most MAX_EACH of one sound play at
+## once (a band of pirates firing), MAX_ALL in all.
+
+const DIR := "res://sounds/"
+const BUS := "SFX"
+const MAX_EACH := 6
+const MAX_ALL := 40
+const MAX_TAKES := 12
+## How far a sound in the world carries (px), and how fast it fades.
+const RANGE := 1500.0
+const FALLOFF := 1.6
+
+var _takes := {}                    # "group/name" -> [AudioStream, ...]
+var _playing := {}                  # "group/name" -> [players]
+var _count := 0
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	if AudioServer.get_bus_index(BUS) < 0:
+		AudioServer.add_bus()
+		var i := AudioServer.bus_count - 1
+		AudioServer.set_bus_name(i, BUS)
+		AudioServer.set_bus_send(i, "Master")
+	apply_volume()
+
+
+## The SFX bus at Settings.sfx_volume (0 = silent, 1 = full).
+func apply_volume() -> void:
+	var i := AudioServer.get_bus_index(BUS)
+	if i < 0:
+		return
+	var v: float = Settings.sfx_volume
+	AudioServer.set_bus_mute(i, v <= 0.001)
+	AudioServer.set_bus_volume_db(i, linear_to_db(maxf(v, 0.001)))
+
+
+## Every take of a sound (loaded once).
+func takes(key: String) -> Array:
+	if not _takes.has(key):
+		var found := []
+		for k in range(1, MAX_TAKES + 1):
+			var path := "%s%s_%d.ogg" % [DIR, key, k]
+			if not ResourceLoader.exists(path):
+				break
+			found.append(load(path))
+		_takes[key] = found
+	return _takes[key]
+
+
+func _free_slot(key: String) -> bool:
+	var live: Array = _playing.get(key, []).filter(func(p): return is_instance_valid(p))
+	_playing[key] = live
+	return live.size() < MAX_EACH and _count < MAX_ALL
+
+
+func _track(key: String, p: Node) -> void:
+	_playing[key].append(p)
+	_count += 1
+	p.tree_exited.connect(func(): _count -= 1)
+
+
+## Plays a sound in the world at `at` (in `parent`'s coordinates): it fades
+## with distance from the camera. volume_db shifts it (quieter footsteps);
+## pitch: how much the pitch may wander (0.06 = +-6 %). Null if it didn't play.
+func play_at(key: String, at: Vector2, parent: Node, volume_db := 0.0, pitch := 0.06) -> AudioStreamPlayer2D:
+	var list := takes(key)
+	if list.is_empty() or parent == null or not parent.is_inside_tree() or not _free_slot(key):
+		return null
+	var p := AudioStreamPlayer2D.new()
+	p.stream = list.pick_random()
+	p.position = at
+	p.bus = BUS
+	p.volume_db = volume_db
+	p.pitch_scale = 1.0 + randf_range(-pitch, pitch)
+	p.max_distance = RANGE
+	p.attenuation = FALLOFF
+	p.finished.connect(p.queue_free)
+	parent.add_child(p)
+	_track(key, p)
+	p.play()
+	return p
+
+
+## Plays a sound at a global position: in the FX layer (group "fx_layer") or
+## else the current scene.
+func play_world(key: String, global_at: Vector2, volume_db := 0.0, pitch := 0.06) -> AudioStreamPlayer2D:
+	var tree := get_tree()
+	var layer: Node = tree.get_first_node_in_group("fx_layer")
+	if layer == null:
+		layer = tree.current_scene
+	if not layer is Node2D:
+		return null
+	return play_at(key, (layer as Node2D).to_local(global_at), layer, volume_db, pitch)
+
+
+## A looping sound on `node` (its first take, looping), playing: it moves with
+## the node and goes when it does. Not counted against the caps; the caller
+## turns it up / down / stops it. Null if the sound doesn't exist.
+func loop_at(key: String, node: Node, volume_db := 0.0, max_distance := RANGE) -> AudioStreamPlayer2D:
+	var list := takes(key)
+	if list.is_empty() or node == null:
+		return null
+	var st: AudioStream = list[0]
+	if st is AudioStreamOggVorbis:
+		st.loop = true
+	var p := AudioStreamPlayer2D.new()
+	p.stream = st
+	p.bus = BUS
+	p.volume_db = volume_db
+	p.max_distance = max_distance
+	p.attenuation = FALLOFF
+	node.add_child(p)
+	if p.is_inside_tree():
+		p.play()
+	else:
+		p.ready.connect(p.play)
+	return p
+
+
+## Plays a sound flat - not in the world (yours: loot you pick up, the UI).
+func play(key: String, volume_db := 0.0, pitch := 0.04) -> AudioStreamPlayer:
+	var list := takes(key)
+	if list.is_empty() or not _free_slot(key):
+		return null
+	var p := AudioStreamPlayer.new()
+	p.stream = list.pick_random()
+	p.bus = BUS
+	p.volume_db = volume_db
+	p.pitch_scale = 1.0 + randf_range(-pitch, pitch)
+	p.finished.connect(p.queue_free)
+	add_child(p)
+	_track(key, p)
+	p.play()
+	return p

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,127 @@ 
+class_name ShipScanner
+extends Node2D
+## Your ship's scanner (right-click in space, main.gd):
+##  - on an asteroid (within ROCK_RANGE): a laser scan sweeps across it for
+##    ROCK_TIME s; when it's done the rock stays highlighted with its kind and
+##    the ore it holds (Asteroid.scanned).
+##  - on empty space: a system scan - rings of energy pulse out from the ship;
+##    then the radar shows arrows to every station and planet for
+##    ARROW_TIME s (Minimap.scan_until).
+## Drawn in the world, above the ships (z_index).
+
+const ROCK_RANGE := 1600.0
+const ROCK_TIME := 1.3
+const WAVE_TIME := 1.8
+const WAVE_RADIUS := 2600.0
+const WAVES := 3
+const ARROW_TIME := 10.0
+const CYAN := Color(0.35, 1.0, 0.9)
+
+var ship: Node2D
+var minimap: Control
+var _rock: Node2D                   # being scanned
+var _rock_t := -1.0
+var _waves_t := -1.0                # system scan: time since it started (-1 none)
+var _wave_from := Vector2.ZERO
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	z_index = 8
+	z_as_relative = false
+
+
+func scanning() -> bool:
+	return _rock_t >= 0.0 or _waves_t >= 0.0
+
+
+## Scans an asteroid (false if it's out of range).
+func scan_rock(rock: Node2D) -> bool:
+	if ship == null or not is_instance_valid(rock):
+		return false
+	if ship.global_position.distance_to(rock.global_position) > ROCK_RANGE:
+		ship.message.emit("Out of scanner range - get within %.1fk of it" % (ROCK_RANGE / 1000.0))
+		return false
+	_rock = rock
+	_rock_t = 0.0
+	Sfx.play_world("space/scan_laser", rock.global_position, -2.0, 0.03)
+	return true
+
+
+## A system scan: energy waves from the ship, then the radar's arrows.
+func scan_system() -> void:
+	if ship == null:
+		return
+	_waves_t = 0.0
+	_wave_from = ship.global_position
+	Sfx.play("space/scan_pulse", -2.0, 0.02)
+
+
+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	if _rock_t >= 0.0:
+		_rock_t += delta
+		if not is_instance_valid(_rock) or not _rock.is_inside_tree():
+			_rock_t = -1.0
+		elif _rock_t >= ROCK_TIME:
+			_rock_t = -1.0
+			_rock.scanned = true
+			Sfx.play("space/scan_done", -4.0)
+			GameLog.post("Scanned: %s - %d %s" % [_rock.display_name, _rock.ore_left, Items.display_name(Asteroid.KINDS[_rock.kind]["ore"])], "info")
+	if _waves_t >= 0.0:
+		_waves_t += delta
+		if ship:
+			_wave_from = ship.global_position
+		if _waves_t >= WAVE_TIME + (WAVES - 1) * 0.28:
+			_waves_t = -1.0
+			if minimap:
+				minimap.scan_until = Time.get_ticks_msec() + int(ARROW_TIME * 1000.0)
+			var st := get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("stations").size()
+			var pl := get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("planet_bodies").size()
+			GameLog.post("System scan: %d stations and %d planets located - see your radar." % [st, pl], "info")
+			Sfx.play("space/scan_done", -4.0)
+	queue_redraw()
+
+
+func _draw() -> void:
+	if _rock_t >= 0.0 and is_instance_valid(_rock) and ship:
+		_draw_rock_scan()
+	if _waves_t >= 0.0:
+		_draw_waves()
+
+
+## A fan of laser light from the ship's nose sweeping across the rock, a
+## bright scan line across it and sparks where it touches.
+func _draw_rock_scan() -> void:
+	var nose: Vector2 = ship.global_transform * Vector2(0, -34.0)
+	var c: Vector2 = _rock.global_position
+	var r: float = _rock.hit_radius
+	var u := _rock_t / ROCK_TIME
+	var dir := nose.direction_to(c)
+	var side := dir.orthogonal()
+	var sweep := sin(u * TAU * 1.5) * 0.9   # back and forth across it
+	var hit := c + side * sweep * r - dir * sqrt(maxf(0.0, 1.0 - sweep * sweep)) * r * 0.6
+	var a := 1.0 - maxf(0.0, u - 0.85) / 0.15
+	draw_colored_polygon(PackedVector2Array([nose, c + side * r - dir * r * 0.2, c - side * r - dir * r * 0.2]), Color(CYAN, 0.08 * a))
+	draw_line(nose, hit, Color(CYAN, 0.9 * a), 2.0, true)
+	draw_line(nose, hit, Color(1, 1, 1, 0.6 * a), 0.8, true)
+	# The scan line across the rock, and a faint grid over it.
+	draw_line(hit - dir * r * 0.9, hit + dir * r * 0.4, Color(CYAN, 0.7 * a), 2.0, true)
+	for k in range(-2, 3):
+		draw_arc(c, r * (0.45 + 0.2 * (k + 2)), 0, TAU, 32, Color(CYAN, 0.12 * a), 1.0, true)
+	draw_circle(hit, 4.0 + 2.0 * sin(_rock_t * 40.0), Color(1, 1, 1, 0.8 * a))
+	# Progress readout.
+	var font := ThemeDB.fallback_font
+	var fs := Settings.fs("world", 13)
+	draw_string(font, c + Vector2(-110, -r * 1.4 - 10.0), "SCANNING  %d%%" % int(u * 100.0), HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER, 220, fs, CYAN)
+
+
+## Rings of energy pulsing out from the ship.
+func _draw_waves() -> void:
+	for k in WAVES:
+		var t := _waves_t - k * 0.28
+		if t < 0.0 or t > WAVE_TIME:
+			continue
+		var u := t / WAVE_TIME
+		var rr := WAVE_RADIUS * (1.0 - pow(1.0 - u, 2.2))
+		var a := (1.0 - u) * 0.85
+		draw_arc(_wave_from, rr, 0, TAU, 128, Color(CYAN, a * 0.35), 26.0 * (1.0 - u) + 4.0, true)
+		draw_arc(_wave_from, rr, 0, TAU, 128, Color(0.85, 1.0, 1.0, a), 2.5, true)

files.explanation: New autoload Voice: plays a dialogue line's Piper recording, found by a hash of the speaker and the line.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,75 @@ 
+extends Node
+## Autoload "Voice": spoken dialogue. Every story line is recorded with
+## Piper (neural text to speech, offline) by tools/voice_lines.py, one voice
+## per character, as res://voices/lines/<key>.ogg - key: the first 16 hex
+## digits of sha1("<speaker>|<the line without BBCode>"). Saying a line plays
+## its own recording:
+##
+##   Voice.speak("Then the thread is in your hands.", "Kilon Alios")
+##   Voice.stop()
+##
+## A line with no recording (edited since, or never recorded) is silent - run
+## tools/voice_lines.py again (test_audio checks every quest line has one).
+## The dialogue box speaks each line as it shows it. Plays on the "Voice"
+## bus (Settings.voice_volume), also while the game is paused.
+
+const DIR := "res://voices/lines/"
+const BUS := "Voice"
+
+var _player: AudioStreamPlayer
+var speaking := ""                  # the key of the line being spoken ("" none)
+static var _bb := RegEx.create_from_string("\\[[^\\]]*\\]")
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS
+	if AudioServer.get_bus_index(BUS) < 0:
+		AudioServer.add_bus()
+		var i := AudioServer.bus_count - 1
+		AudioServer.set_bus_name(i, BUS)
+		AudioServer.set_bus_send(i, "Master")
+	_player = AudioStreamPlayer.new()
+	_player.bus = BUS
+	_player.process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS
+	_player.finished.connect(func(): speaking = "")
+	add_child(_player)
+	apply_volume()
+
+
+## The Voice bus at Settings.voice_volume (0 = silent).
+func apply_volume() -> void:
+	var i := AudioServer.get_bus_index(BUS)
+	if i < 0:
+		return
+	var v: float = Settings.voice_volume
+	AudioServer.set_bus_mute(i, v <= 0.001)
+	AudioServer.set_bus_volume_db(i, linear_to_db(maxf(v, 0.001)))
+
+
+## The recording's key for a line (as tools/voice_lines.py names it).
+static func key(text: String, speaker: String) -> String:
+	var plain := _bb.sub(text, "", true).strip_edges()
+	return ("%s|%s" % [speaker, plain]).sha1_text().substr(0, 16)
+
+
+## The recording of a line (null if it has none).
+static func recording(text: String, speaker: String) -> AudioStream:
+	var path := DIR + key(text, speaker) + ".ogg"
+	return load(path) if ResourceLoader.exists(path) else null
+
+
+## Speaks a line (stopping whatever was being said); silent if it has no recording.
+func speak(text: String, speaker: String) -> void:
+	stop()
+	var st := recording(text, speaker)
+	if st == null:
+		return
+	speaking = key(text, speaker)
+	_player.stream = st
+	_player.play()
+
+
+func stop() -> void:
+	if _player and _player.playing:
+		_player.stop()
+	speaking = ""
hunks.title: Voice
hunks.note: speak() looks up voices/lines/<key>.ogg and plays it on the Voice bus; lines without one are silent.

bubbles.text: BBCode tags ([b], [color]...) are stripped first, so styling a line doesn't lose its recording.
The same key tools/voice_lines.py names the files by: change a line and it has a new key - silent until recorded.
One voice at a time: a new line cuts off the last.
Dialogue pauses the game, so the voice must play while paused.
